title: Hierarchically Porous Polyaniline Film via Interfacial Self-Assembly for Ultrafast Dual-Band Electrochromic Smart Window
abstract: Abstract Dual-band electrochromic smart windows, capable of independently regulating visible and near-infrared solar radiation, offer an effective route toward reducing building/vehicle energy consumption. However, their practical implementation is often limited by slow switching kinetics, insufficient bistability, as well as challenges in fabricating polychromatic, uniform, and scalable electrochromic films with efficient ion and charge transport. Here, we report an interfacial self-assembly strategy to fabricate large-area polyaniline (PANI) thin films featuring a hierarchically porous architecture and thickness-dependent porosity gradient. The self-assembly process, driven by solvent exchange at the air–water interface and modulated by surfactant confinement, produces interconnected PANI nanoparticle networks with both in-plane hierarchical pores and out-of-plane structural gradation. This architecture facilitates electrolyte penetration and charge transport across the film thickness. As a result, the PANI films enable rapid and stable dual-band electrochromic modulation, exhibiting three distinct optical states (“bright”, “cool”, and “dark”) with independent control of visible and near-infrared transmittance. The assembled devices demonstrate fast response (coloration/bleaching times of 1.8/4 s at 633 nm and 1.2/3.6 s at 1200 nm), high coloration efficiency, and excellent optical bistability, together with effective indoor thermal regulation. These results establish interfacial self-assembly as a versatile approach for engineering functional polymer films for next-generation energy-efficient smart windows.

title: Programmable Microgel Degradation in Dynamic Granular Hydrogels Guides Extracellular Matrix Assembly During Tissue Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Granular hydrogels have attracted widespread interest for wound healing applications, yet their static design, in which microstructure and void space remain fixed, contrasts with the dynamic nature of tissue repair where processes like provisional extracellular matrix (pECM) assembly, cell organization, and nascent tissue formation evolve over time. Here, this disparity is addressed by designing dynamic granular hydrogels that are modularly assembled using microgels with pre‐programmed and precise degradation rates ranging from a few days to several weeks. Microgel degradation is controlled via modulation of hydrolytic susceptibility of hyaluronic acid polymers. The biological significance of timed pore expansion in dynamic granular hydrogels is investigated in a mouse muscle crush injury model. While slow‐degrading hydrogels support a distinct spatial assembly of cell‐instructive interstitial matrix and basement membrane proteins in the expanded pore space, this pECM remodeling is adversely altered in non‐degrading or fast‐degrading hydrogels. Slow‐degrading dynamic granular hydrogels also show long‐term therapeutic benefits on muscle wound healing, evidenced by reduced fibrosis, enhanced myogenesis, and improved functional force recovery. Collectively, these striking results demonstrate the profound significance of incorporating dynamicity through controlled microgel degradation in advanced granular biomaterials to improve tissue repair outcomes.

title: Brick‐Layer Templating of (002)‐Oriented Zn at Battery Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising candidates for future large‐scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost. However, dendritic Zn growth at the anode severely compromises its long‐term cyclability and thus impedes practical deployment of AZIBs. From a crystallographic perspective, enforcing preferential Zn growth along the (002) orientation can effectively suppress dendrite formation, but most existing strategies rely on pre‐texturing of anodes or substantially altering the electrolyte composition, both of which add additional complexity and cost. In this regard, achieving robust (002)‐oriented Zn deposition on commercial Zn foil in a ZnSO 4 ‐dominated electrolyte remains crucial to the future development of AZIBs. Herein, we develop a new electrolyte additive, 2,4,6‐trimethoxy‐s‐triazine (TST), which functions at trace concentrations to enable (002)‐oriented Zn deposition at battery anodes. Via pre‐adsorption on the anode surface, TST promotes a hexagonally ordered Zn adlayer as an interfacial brick template, thereby enabling texture‐inherited (002) plating during subsequent electrodeposition. The proposed mechanism is corroborated through multi‐dimensional characterization, and the resulting Zn anodes deliver markedly improved cycling stability across multiple cell configurations. We believe this work can inspire future studies on crystallographic orientation engineering‐based Zn anode protection and can accelerate the practical implementation of AZIBs.

title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

title: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

title: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
abstract: Abstract The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

title: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
abstract: Abstract Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves &gt;90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.

title: Biocompatible mesoporous silica particles for enzyme immobilization: A review
abstract: Enzyme immobilization within mesoporous silica is a powerful strategy for improving biocatalyst stability, reusability, and process economics in industrial applications. Conventional mesoporous silica materials, such as MCM-41 and SBA-15, possess high surface area, tunable pore size, and excellent thermal stability; however, their synthesis typically relies on surfactant templates and harsh calcination procedures that are incompatible with fragile biomolecules and sustainable manufacturing. In contrast, biocompatible mesoporous silica prepared through non-surfactant templating employs mild extraction conditions compatible with one-pot enzyme immobilization and direct hydrogel coating. The properties of biocompatible mesoporous silica particles (BMSP) can be further enhanced through surface engineering using silane coupling agents, crosslinking chemistry, and silanol density enhancement to improve enzyme–support interactions and immobilization efficiency. Hybrid architectures incorporating magnetic materials, organic polymers, carbonaceous supports, metal oxides, and hierarchical pore networks further expand BMSP functionality by enabling catalyst recovery, enhanced biocompatibility, improved structural robustness, and superior mass transport. However, these engineering strategies may also introduce diffusion limitations, enzyme conformational changes, and additional material and processing burdens that can significantly affect biocatalytic performance and environmental sustainability. This review systematically examines the structure–performance relationships associated with these challenges and evaluates the environmental implications of non-surfactant synthesis, surface functionalization, and hybrid material integration. Mitigation strategies, including larger non-surfactant templates, hierarchical meso-macroporous architectures, and optimized surface functionalization, are discussed to alleviate diffusion limitations and preserve enzyme structure. Quantitative descriptors, including the Thiele modulus, effectiveness factor, Michaelis constant (Km), and maximum reaction rate (Vmax), are highlighted as engineering tools for evaluating support performance and guiding rational materials design. This review provides a framework for developing next-generation biocompatible mesoporous silica platforms for sustainable industrial biocatalysis.

title: Constructing the Transfer Ladder between Active Sites and Functional Units within the Cluster-Based Catalyst for Reductive Amination
abstract: Abstract The remote communication between active sites and the surrounding environment within a heterogeneous catalyst for the orderly bonding of reactive species is highly desired yet very challenging. Here we find that the phosphotungstate with a mesoporous framework (abbreviated as mPTA) has an extraordinary ability to accommodate ammonia but has no activity for catalytic reductive amination, while the Pd3(S-Adm)3(PPh3)3+ (Pd3 for short; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiol) cluster enables the above reaction but insufficient ammonia occurring on the cluster leads to low activity and inferior selectivity. We thereby construct a transfer channel between the active cluster (Pd3) and the functional unit (mPTA), which is identified as an interfacial ladder of Pd–O–W, delivering ammonia molecules from the functional unit to the active center. The mPTA resembles a pump source to supply ammonia to meet the requirement for the reductive amination over the cluster, in which ammonia hops the ladder to expediently react with H2 and carbonyl compounds awaiting on Pd sites, finally giving rise to remarkable performances with a high yield of amines. We recognize that the interactive cooperation of inner catalysis with peripheral input across two different compounds holds promise in decoupling and controlling complex chemical ecosystems for high-quality productivity.

title: Hierarchical Descriptor-Driven Machine Learning Reveals the Structure–Performance Landscape of Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks for CO 2 /N 2 Separation
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs) are emerging as promising adsorbents for postcombustion CO2 capture owing to their mild self-assembly, solution processability, and facile regeneration, yet the structural and chemical factors governing their separation performance remain poorly resolved. Here, we report an integrated computational workflow combining high-throughput GCMC simulation, interpretable machine learning, and atomistic mechanism analysis to evaluate 84,261 HOFs for CO2/N2 separation under simulated flue-gas conditions. After benchmarking against experimental isotherms, a hierarchical four-level descriptor set spanning geometric, thermodynamic, elemental, and chemical/electronic features was constructed. Among eight algorithms, XGBoost delivered the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.93), and both feature importance and SHAP analyses identified geometric and thermodynamic descriptors as the dominant determinants of selectivity. High-performance HOFs converge on a common signature of smaller pores, denser frameworks, and enriched polar hydrogen-bond-donating groups (amino and carboxyl moieties), which cooperatively strengthen framework-CO2 interactions and widen the CO2/N2 heat-of-adsorption gap. Three-dimensional density mapping and geometry-based hydrogen-bond statistics confirm that preferential framework-CO2 hydrogen bonding is the key microscopic driving force, whereas N2 remains uniformly dispersed and forms essentially no effective hydrogen bonds. This work provides a high-fidelity predictive model and transferable design rules that advance HOF-based CO2/N2 separation from isolated breakthroughs toward mechanism-guided systematic design.

title: Regulating Energy Dissipation Pathways in Rare‐Earth D‐D′‐A MOFs for High Sensitivity X‐Ray Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct X‐ray detectors are of great importance for high‐performance X‐ray imaging, yet semiconductive metal‐organic framework (MOF)‐based detectors remain limited by inefficient charge transport and additional energy loss during irradiation. Herein, we construct two isostructural ternary D‐D′‐A rare‐earth polyoxometalate MOF single crystals, Tm‐NDI‐SiW and Eu‐NDI‐SiW, in which the rare‐earth nodes, [SiW 12 O 40 ] 4− , and H 4 BINDI function as the donor (D), secondary donor (D′), and acceptor (A), respectively, enabling long‐range charge‐transfer channels and efficient carrier separation. Although the two crystals share the same framework architecture, Tm‐NDI‐SiW exhibits strongly suppressed rare‐earth‐related radioluminescence, accompanied by denser molecular packing and stronger donor‐acceptor coupling, thereby reducing radiative energy dissipation and promoting charge collection. As a result, the Tm‐NDI‐SiW single‐crystal detector delivers a sensitivity of 2616.9 µC Gy air −1 cm −2 and a µτ of 8.17 × 10 −5 cm 2 V −1 , approximately 2.0‐ and 1.9‐fold those of Eu‐NDI‐SiW, respectively. Furthermore, incorporating Tm‐NDI‐SiW microcrystals into a PVDF matrix affords a flexible detector with an enhanced sensitivity of 2825.6 µC Gy air −1 cm −2 and enables 3 × 5 pixel X‐ray imaging. These results show that regulating radioluminescence as a competing energy‐dissipation pathway, together with promoting long‐range charge transport, is an effective strategy for high‐performance MOF‐based direct X‐ray detection.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
abstract: Abstract Intermolecular Diels–Alder (DA) cycloadditions are pivotal for constructing complex polycyclic architectures. However, biological catalysts performing this transformation on diketopiperazine (DKP) cores remain largely unidentified. Here, we report a decentralized biosynthetic pathway in the deep-sea cold-seep sourced fungus Aspergillus chevalieri CS-122 that assembles chevalinulin A, a spiro[bicyclo[2.2.2]octane]-DKP alkaloid. This pathway involves two nonclustered enzymes, CalO and FadA. CalO is a cytochrome P450 that furnishes an essential exocyclic olefin, while FadA represents the first FAD oxidoreductase-like Diels–Alderase that catalyzes an intermolecular, endoselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition between neoechinulin B and 3,4-trans-cyclohexadiene. These enzymes function downstream of a conserved gene cluster, effectively decoupling core scaffold assembly from late-stage functionalization. This strategy likely underpins the extensive structural diversity of fungal DKP alkaloids. Notably, CalO and FadA were identified via an integrated transcriptomic and structure-guided computational pipeline, rather than sequence homology, demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in mining functional catalysts from genomic “dark matter”. Mutational analysis indicates that residues M193, Y226, Y315, and D446 are critical in FadA activity. This study reveals a decentralized biosynthetic paradigm linking clustered core assembly with dispersed diversification, establishing a general framework for engineering complex alkaloid scaffolds.

title: Regulating Platinum Utilization and Intrinsic Hydrogen Evolution Activity via Carbon Pore Architecture
abstract: Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a key process for sustainable hydrogen production. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the high cost and inefficient utilization of platinum (Pt). Here, we investigated the influence of carbon pore architecture on Pt dispersion and intrinsic catalytic activity using a series of porous carbons spanning narrow mesoporous (MH and MH‐18; 2–5 nm), wider mesoporous (MJ010 and MJ030; 10–40 nm), and macroporous (MJ150; ~110 nm) frameworks. Pt nanoparticles formed via microwave‐assisted polyol reduction showed uniform nucleation. Macroporous MJ150 stabilizes ~2.3 nm Pt nanoparticles while preserving porosity, whereas narrow mesoporous carbons promote confinement and pore blockage, with XRD/Raman confirming higher crystallinity. XPS further shows a dominant metallic Pt 0 state with minimal Pt–O interactions on the macroporous support. Electrochemical measurements reveal that Pt/MJ150 exhibits superior HER performance, delivering an overpotential of 20 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , and higher mass activity than commercial Pt/C. C dl , ECSA, ICP‐OES, durability, post‐HER XRD and XPS measurements confirm improved active‐site accessibility and Pt utilization, through mass transport. Overall, this study shows a clear structural–property–performance relationship, where macroporous carbon supports enable efficient Pt utilization at low loading provide a scalable strategy for HER.

title: Framework Bond Chemistry Governs Seed Activity through Molecular Precursor Regulation in SSZ-39 Crystallization
abstract: Abstract Seed-assisted synthesis is widely used to accelerate zeolite crystallization, yet the molecular origin of differences in seed activity remains unclear. Here, we show that seed activity in SSZ-39 crystallization is governed by framework bond chemistry and its control over the dissolved molecular precursor ensemble. By combining Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS ssNMR) spectroscopy, crystallization kinetics, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we compare SAPO-18, NH4A, homologous SSZ-39, and seed-free systems. All systems yield phase-pure AEI zeolite, but their crystallization rates differ sharply: SAPO-18 completes crystallization within 12 h, approximately six times faster than the seed-free system. FT-ICR MS reveals that active seeds shift aluminosilicate precursors toward low-condensation oligomers (&lt;6 T atoms) and enrich the corresponding OSDA-associated complexes. DFT calculations show that these low-condensation aluminosilicates interact more strongly with DMDMP cations than more highly condensed counterparts, linking precursor speciation to OSDA utilization and nucleation. The exceptional activity of SAPO-18 arises from facile alkaline hydrolysis of weak P–O–Al linkages, which promotes extensive seed dissolution, while the released phosphate remains outside the SSZ-39 framework. In contrast, stronger Si–O–Al and Si–O–Si linkages in aluminosilicate seeds limit dissolution and generate less favorable precursor ensembles. These results identify framework bond chemistry as a molecular descriptor of seed activity and recast zeolite seeds as chemical regulators rather than passive structural templates, providing a basis for rational and lower-OSDA zeolite synthesis.

title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
abstract: Abstract Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence 1,2 . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly 3,4 . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics 5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design 7 and processable materials 8–10 .

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as O ‐glycosylated or O ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc ‐(NH 4 ) 2 Hg(SCN) 4 ( Cc ‐AHT) and its C 2/ c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN) − ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS 4 ] core throughout the [Hg(SCN) 4 ] 2− module, establishing an atomic‐shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc ‐AHT exhibits a giant second‐harmonic generation response (14 × KH 2 PO 4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO 4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δ n = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter‐sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1 , COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H + /4e – ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3 . The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm −2 , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

title: High-order nanofluidic spiking encoding
abstract: Abstract High-order memristor is needed in neuromorphic engineering for sophisticated neural encoding. Progress has been made in solid-state memristor with electronic dynamics, which, however, presents a significant disparity with the ionic-chemical signaling in the human brain. Herein, we realize high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding based on synergizing the high porosity for non-linear ion transport, light responsibility for optical sensing, and catalytic chemistry for biological perception of a multifunctional covalent organic framework under nanoconfinement. The unique multimodal responses make possible the co-encoded spiking by electricity, light and real neurotransmitter glutamate in the physiological media, leading to the significantly enriched synaptic plasticity towards high-order spiking encoding behaviors, i.e. the rate encoding, time-to-first-spike encoding, rate and temporal fusion encoding, and history-dependent spiking encoding. It is expected to be a starting point for high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding.

title: Fluoride-Enabled Assembly of Iron–Hydrogen-Bonded Frameworks as Bifunctional Lewis Acid–Base Catalysts for Knoevenagel Condensation
abstract: Abstract The development of recyclable heterogeneous catalysts that enable efficient organic transformations without solvents is important for sustainable chemical synthesis. In this work, two new fluoride-mediated metal–hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (M-HOFs), labeled as JOU-40 and JOU-41, were successfully synthesized. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both M-HOFs feature [Fe3F11]n chains that are extended into three-dimensional supramolecular networks through O–H···F hydrogen bonds. The resulting frameworks integrate Lewis-acidic iron centers and basic fluoride sites within a confined porous environment, enabling efficient Lewis acid–base catalysis. As heterogeneous catalysts, JOU-40 and JOU-41 efficiently promote the solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation of benzaldehyde with malononitrile, affording &gt;99.00% conversion and selectivity. The catalyst also exhibits good substrate compatibility across a range of substituted aldehydes. More fascinatingly, kinetic analyses reveal that the reaction can be described by the Avrami nucleation–growth model, highlighting the coupled contributions of chemical conversion and product crystallization. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that the adjacent Fe3+ and F– sites activate the two reactants and facilitate C═C bond formation, providing a molecular-level basis for the observed catalytic activity. This work offers new design insights for developing highly efficient, stable, and recyclable catalytic systems for solvent-free Knoevenagel condensation.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O 2 . A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O 2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Adsorption Mechanisms of RNA on Advanced Porous Materials: Current Status and Future Perspectives in Environmental Remediation and Biosafety
abstract: Environmental RNA (eRNA), derived from living organisms, pathogens, and double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)-based biopesticides, is becoming increasingly important in the contexts of environmental monitoring, biosafety, and environmental remediation. Although RNA is considered an unstable molecule, its stability can increase through interactions with solid surfaces and porous materials, thereby influencing its transport, accumulation, and bioavailability in the environment. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge regarding RNA adsorption onto advanced porous materials, including metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), mesoporous silica, carbon-based materials, biochar, porous polymers, and hybrid materials. It outlines RNA binding mechanisms—such as electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, π–π interactions, and metal-ion complexation—as well as the influence of environmental factors such as pH, ionic strength, and the presence of organic substances. Methods for studying RNA adsorption, adsorbent regeneration and reusability, and potential applications in wastewater treatment, environmental monitoring, and the mitigation of the spread of biologically active RNA are also discussed. This review highlights the persistent gap between laboratory-scale adsorption studies and the real-world deployment of RNA-capturing materials in complex environmental matrices and proposes an integrative framework tracing how RNA type and material properties jointly shape adsorption mechanisms and, in turn, biosafety outcomes.

title: pH-Responsive Supramolecular Self-Assembly of an Aromatic Zwitterionic Surfactant-Polyamine System for High-Temperature Clean Fracturing Fluids
abstract: Abstract To address the thermal limitations inherent to conventional viscoelastic surfactant (VES) fracturing fluids, a novel aromatic zwitterionic surfactant, erucamidopropyl dimethyl carboxybenzyl ammonium chloride (ECBA), was synthesized and formulated with diethylenetriamine (DETA) to construct a supramolecular clean fracturing fluid (CFF) system. Comprehensive rheological evaluations revealed that the ECBA/DETA system achieved optimal performance at a total concentration of 4.0 wt % and pH 3.95. Mechanistically, the pH-responsive protonation of the carboxyl and amino moieties synergistically reinforced intermolecular electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonding, driving the self-assembly of a robust supramolecular network. Cryo-SEM observation, combined with DLS measurements and packing parameter analysis, revealed a distinct porous network morphology and provided complementary evidence for the pH-dependent self-assembly and viscoelasticity of the system. Consequently, the optimized fluid exhibited elastic-dominated viscoelastic behavior with outstanding thermal and shear stability up to 110 °C. At 90 °C, the proppant settling velocity was remarkably suppressed to 0.750 cm/min, indicating superior proppant-carrying capacity. Furthermore, the incorporation of a DTPA chelating agent significantly enhanced the system’s resistance to Ca2+ ions. Regarding reservoir protection, complete gel breaking was achieved within 1 h using 10% kerosene at 90 °C, yielding an ultralow residue content of 0.147 mg/L. The resulting gel breaking fluid displayed reduced surface and interfacial tensions (22.7 and 0.051 mN/m, respectively), a high clay antiswelling efficiency of 85%, and favorable emulsification/demulsification behavior. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the synergistic noncovalent interactions between the aromatic zwitterionic surfactant and DETA under acidic conditions effectively stabilize the supramolecular network, providing a promising molecular design strategy for high-temperature and formation-friendly CFFs.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
abstract: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.

title: Framework-Templated Single Clathrate Hydrate Cages in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Molecular simulations identify metal–organic framework (MOF) pores that retain single methane hydrate cages and, for a nonstandard 16-water cage, support its assembly from disordered water. In smooth spherical pores, a methane molecule assembled twenty waters into the pentagonal dodecahedron of structure I hydrate and sixteen waters into a 435661 cage, a polyhedron that no known hydrate crystal contains. These idealized models were built by language-model agents and then walked back toward real materials, an approach referred to here as agentic doodling, and they guided a screening of 120,419 experimental MOF structures. Most size-matched pores pulled the cage apart, but a small set of frameworks kept it intact at 216 K, better with methane than without, and ELOZIQ kept the dodecahedron up to 270 K, near the melting temperature of the water model. In XODDED and GUQMAH, the nonstandard cage was held at least as well as in an ideal spherical pore, and it self-assembled around methane from randomly placed water, with nearly all of its edges hydrogen bonded. The pores template the cages through a moderate attraction spread over the cage corners rather than through strong binding sites placed at the corners. These results open a route to designing MOFs that hold single hydrate cages, including cages that do not occur in bulk hydrates.

title: Hidden Structures and Unusual Fourth-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions Drive Atomic Ordering in Thermoelectric AgSbTe2
abstract: Abstract AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) &gt; 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along &lt;100&gt;. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along &lt;100&gt; arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

title: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
abstract: Abstract Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (&gt;80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

title: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
abstract: Abstract Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor– π –acceptor (D– π –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate ( M1 ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π ‐conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π ‐conjugation.

title: Rational Construction of Flexible-Rigid β-Cyclodextrin Cross-Linked Porous Microspheres for High-Efficiency Oil Absorption
abstract: Abstract Oil spills and toxic organic solvent leakage damage aquatic environments and human health, while traditional polymer oil adsorbents feature disconnected pores, weak recyclability, and conflicting adsorption capacity and structural stability. Herein, renewable β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) was esterified into a multivinyl cross-linker (β-CD-A), and flexible-rigid balanced porous DBP microspheres were synthesized via one-pot suspension copolymerization. Gradient monomer screening identified 35 mol % rigid comonomer 4-tert-butylstyrene (PTBS) as the optimal dosage. Dodecane served as a porogen to build interconnected hierarchical macro/meso/micropores, endowing DBP with high adsorption capacities of 135.6, 128.8, and 115.1 g g–1 for CCl4, CHCl3, and toluene. Adsorption obeys pseudo-first-order kinetics, driven by capillary force and van der Waals force. After 10 adsorption–desorption cycles, the microspheres reserve over 75% initial capacity, perform steadily from −20 to 60 °C, and lose less than 6% mass in water, concentrated acid, and alkali. This work demonstrates a flexible-rigid synergistic approach for fabricating hierarchically porous β-CD adsorbents. The scalable material shows potential for marine oil spill remediation and industrial organic wastewater treatment.

title: Fluorophore-Conjugated Diphenylalanine Peptides Reveal Self-Sorting in a Multicomponent Supramolecular System
abstract: The interplay between distinct molecular building blocks in multicomponent supramolecular systems can lead to co-assembly or self-sorting, yet distinguishing between these modes of organization remains challenging. Here, we developed two intrinsically fluorescent derivatives of the self-assembling dipeptide diphenylalanine (FF): nitrobenzoxadiazole-conjugated FF (NBD-FF) and a coumarin-conjugated tert-butyloxycarbonyl-protected FF derivative (BocFF-DAC). Both derivatives formed fibrillar assemblies while exhibiting spectrally distinct fluorescence, enabling their direct visualization by confocal microscopy. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of NBD-FF revealed an extended hydrogen-bonded lattice in which the NBD moiety participates directly in intermolecular interactions, including aromatic, hydrophobic, and hydrogen-bonding contacts. This finding demonstrates that the fluorophore acts as an active structural element rather than a passive label. When NBD-FF and BocFF-DAC were assembled together, confocal microscopy revealed predominantly spatially distinct fibrillar populations with limited overlap, consistent with preferential self-sorting rather than uniform co-assembly. These findings establish fluorophore-conjugated short peptides as intrinsically traceable building blocks for investigating multicomponent supramolecular organization, while highlighting that fluorophore conjugation can simultaneously enable visualization and influence the assembly.

title: Tuning Coordination Chemistry and Composition of Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the cost and efficiency of hydrogen production via water splitting is a long‐standing research challenge in support of carbon neutrality goals. Optimising the structural composition and coordination chemistry of metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) can yield suitable catalysts or supports that enhance hydrogen production efficiency. MOFs offer precise control over porosity, metal nodes and linker chemistry that is unattainable with conventional catalysts. This review provides a critical, cross‐cutting assessment of MOF‐based catalysis across electrochemical (EC) and photo(electro)chemical (PC and PEC) water‐splitting technologies. We systematically analyse how key structural features (ultrahigh porosity, surface area and compositional changes) and coordination chemistry (tunable metal active sites and functionalised linkers) govern catalytic activity and stability. For electrochemical systems, we critically examine the multifunctionality of pristine MOFs, their conductive carbon‐based derivatives and the synergistic performance of MOF/carbon and MOF/metal hybrids. For MOF‐driven PC and PEC water splitting, we examine MOF selectivity and the mechanisms of light absorption, charge separation and interfacial electron transfer that enable MOFs to serve as integrated platforms bridging light harvesting and redox catalysis. Notably, we devote dedicated sections to limitations in charge‐carrier dynamics and defect engineering, significant bottlenecks that are often overlooked yet key to future performance breakthroughs. A machine‐learning perspective is briefly included, with case studies presented as an emerging design tool for predicting hydrogen adsorption capacity and optimising hydrogen production activity via MOF‐based catalysts. Finally, the review concludes with targeted future directions aimed at accelerating the transition from laboratory discovery to practical, sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Photothermal conversion and utilization in solar-driven interfacial water evaporation
abstract: Abstract Global water scarcity and increasing energy demand have created an urgent need for sustainable and energy-efficient freshwater-production technologies. Solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SIE) localizes solar absorption, heat generation, and vaporization near the water–air interface, thereby reducing ineffective bulk-water heating. However, SIE performance is determined not only by the amount of solar radiation absorbed but also by how the absorbed photon energy is converted into heat, transported to interfacial water, and ultimately translated into vapor and collected freshwater. This review therefore establishes a mechanism-to-device-to-water framework linking microscopic photothermal conversion with system-level energy utilization. The heat-generation mechanisms of major photothermal material classes are discussed, including localized surface plasmon resonance in metallic nanomaterials, carrier thermalization and nonradiative recombination in semiconductors, electronic excitation and phonon-mediated dissipation in carbon materials, excited-state nonradiative relaxation in organic molecules and conductive polymers, and free-carrier absorption and electronic–phononic dissipation in MXenes. Developments in COFs, MOFs, and hybrid photothermal systems are also examined. Beyond material-level conversion, the review analyzes how solar absorptance, mid-infrared thermal emittance, heat localization, water supply, vapor diffusion, salt management, and multiscale architecture collectively govern evaporation. An energy-flow framework is introduced to distinguish solar absorptance, intrinsic light-to-heat conversion efficiency, solar-to-vapor efficiency, and water-collection efficiency, while addressing environmental heat uptake, dark-evaporation correction, and evaporation-enthalpy interpretation. The integration of evaporation, condensation, freshwater collection, and all-day operation through radiative cooling or auxiliary Joule heating is further considered. Finally, standardized testing, cost, long-term stability, scalability, and system-level water productivity are identified as key requirements for translating advances in photothermal conversion into reliable freshwater-production technologies.

title: An Environmental Stable Ionogel‐Based Smart Glove System for Integrated Underwater Communication and Safety Warning
abstract: Flexible sensing technology based on hydrogel-based smart gloves enables accurate gesture recognition in complex environments, but such gloves degrade in dry, high-temperature, and underwater conditions, and their complex assembly limits practical usability. Here, a smart glove monitoring system is developed by integrating a poly(benzyl methacrylate-co-2-hydroxyethyl acrylate)/ionic liquid (P(BZMA-co-HEA)/IL) ionogel sensing layer with a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB). The ionogel is constructed through a network-constrained ionic soft-space regulation strategy, where HEA-rich segments strengthen the network, IL provides deformation-adaptive ionic soft spaces, and BZMA-rich hydrophobic segments suppress water penetration. The optimized ionogel combines stretchability (up to 1100%), weight retention (98.86% at room temperature and 95.25% at 65°C), favorable adhesion, anti-swelling behavior, and stable sensing performance under multiple environmental conditions. The FPCB enables a detachable and reconfigurable sensor array, ensuring stable interfacial contact and wearing flexibility. By further combining multi-channel signal acquisition, fully connected neural network (FCNN)-assisted gesture classification, and real-time alert feedback, the smart glove functions as an integrated sensing-recognition-warning platform, achieving 99.92% gesture recognition accuracy and enabling reliable underwater communication and safety warning. This work establishes an effective material design and integration strategy for environmentally adaptive smart gloves.

title: Thermally Induced Structural Transformation in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework
abstract: A long-standing structural question in triphenylene-based conductive metal-organic frameworks is why closely related materials adopt either fully extended honeycomb lattices or intercalated structures containing alternating extended layers and discrete metal–ligand clusters. Ni(II)–HHTP and Co(II)–HHTP (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) have both been reported to have the latter “intercalated structure”, but here we discover that thermal activation and dehydration convert both frameworks to the fully extended structures. Focusing on Ni(II)–HHTP, we show that this structural transformation is reversible, with roomtemperature hydration restoring the intercalated structure. Variable-temperature synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction supports the intercalated-to-fully-extended structural transformation, while solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and elemental analysis provide evidence for the accompanying dehydration. Rehydration of Ni(II)–HHTP restores the intercalated structure, establishing reversible structural switching through removal and reincorporation of water. The resulting change in interlayer architecture alters electrical conductivity, gas response and adsorption properties in Ni(II)–HHTP. Importantly, common sample pre-treatment and testing conditions can themselves change the type of framework structure, meaning that measured properties may not correspond to the initially assigned structure. Because thermal and hydration history determine structure and function, careful structural verification under measurement conditions is, therefore, essential for establishing reliable structure–property relationships. Ultimately our findings resolve a persistent structural ambiguity in this family of materials and allow access to new fully extended electrically conductive framework materials.

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
abstract: ABSTRACT Iron‐sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF‐like nanosheets termed Organic Iron‐Sulfur Frameworks (OISF). Comprehensive characterization, including Mössbauer spectroscopy have confirmed the crystal structure of OISF containing [2Fe‐2S] cores. The OISF exhibits robust electron transfer capability toward various acceptors, mediated by the dynamic formation of interlayer S─S bonds. Leveraging this property, OISF is combined with chloroplasts to enhance dark reactions in vitro and applied as a fertilizer to promote the growth of spinach in vivo, highlighting the potential of stable ISCs in biochemical and industrial applications.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
abstract: Abstract The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned- acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D 2h ligands with lower-symmetry C 2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned- acs ), with a general formula of [M 3 O( L1 ) 3 ]( L2 ) 1/3 . The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C 2 H 2 /CO 2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg −1 vs 0.98 mol kg −1 ).

title: Solvent‐Free Metal–Organic Framework‐Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh‐Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H 2 O solvents, which enables long‐term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO‐66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non‐flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO‐66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination‐dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra‐long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state‐of‐the‐art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V 2 O 5 batteries deliver stable performance across 25−180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high‐temperature Zn||I 2 batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V 2 O 5 batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long‐standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.

title: A Curcumin‐Loaded Iron‐Porphyrin Covalent Organic Framework Alleviates Atherosclerosis by Modulating Oxidative Stress and Lipid Metabolism
abstract: ABSTRACT Atherosclerosis (AS) requires multi‐target therapies addressing lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and inflammation, yet lipid‐lowering alone insufficiently mitigates residual cardiovascular risk. Curcumin (Cur), a natural polyphenol with well‐established anti‐atherosclerotic activities, is severely hampered by extremely low oral bioavailability and rapid metabolic clearance. To overcome these limitations, an iron porphyrin‐based covalent organic framework (COF), FeTAPP‐Dha, was prepared by condensing 5,10,15,20‐tetrakis‐(4‐aminophenyl)‐porphyrin‐Fe‐(III) chloride with 2,5‐dihydroxyterephthalaldehyde. Cur was then incorporated into the hydrophobic channels of FeTAPP‐Dha through hydrogen‐bond‐mediated size matching, producing FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur with a loading efficiency of 12.5%. The incorporated iron porphyrin units provide reactive oxygen species scavenging capability, enabling sustained H 2 O 2 decomposition and intercepting oxidative stress at its source. Moreover, the acidic microenvironment characteristic of atherosclerotic plaques impairs hydrogen‐bonding interactions, facilitating on‐demand Cur release at lesion sites while minimizing systemic exposure. In ApoE −/− mice, FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur effectively inhibited foam cell formation and significantly reduced aortic plaque burden. These effects were accompanied by activation of the AMP‐activated protein kinase–acetyl‐CoA carboxylase signaling axis and suppression of inflammation. Collectively, FeTAPP‐Dha‐Cur achieved superior therapeutic outcomes compared with free Cur or empty carrier. This work establishes a COF‐based synergistic platform that integrates carrier‐mediated microenvironment regulation with stimuli‐responsive drug delivery, offering a promising paradigm for multi‐target AS therapy.

title: Position‐Resolved Fluorescence Polarization Maps Segmental Rigidity in Block Copolymer Micelles in Aqueous and Biological Media
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric micelles are widely used as nanoscale compartments for delivery, sensing, and soft‐matter applications, yet their performance is governed not only by size and morphology but also by the local mobility of polymer segments within the assembly. Here, we describe a position‐resolved fluorescence polarization strategy to map apparent segmental rigidity within block copolymer micelles. By covalently installing the same dansyl fluorophore at defined positions along an amphiphilic block copolymer chain, we selectively label the hydrophobic core, core‐corona interface, and oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG)‐rich corona of the micelles. The resulting fluorescence polarization profiles reveal a pronounced core‐to‐corona apparent rigidity gradient in water, distinguish block‐segregated micelles from compositionally matched random copolymer assemblies, and report micellar responses to temperature, cosolvent, and salt. This method further enables structural interrogation of polymer micelles in biologically relevant media, revealing the unexpected finding that biological serum exerts opposing effects on apparent chain rigidity in the micellar core and corona. Together, these results establish position‐resolved fluorescence polarization as a practical platform for linking block copolymer structure, self‐assembly, local chain dynamics, and biological stability, opening new opportunities to rationally design micelles with environment‐responsive mechanical properties.

title: Hierarchical Porosity Redirects Fe/ZSM-5 from Adsorption-Assisted Removal Toward Fenton/Photo-Fenton Oxidation
abstract: Hierarchical porosity and iron speciation govern the balance between adsorption and catalytic oxidation in Fe-modified ZSM-5. This study compares a microporous low-iron material, Z0–Fe0.1 (0.9 wt.% Fe), with a hierarchically porous high-iron material, Z0.4–Fe1.0 (25 wt.% Fe). Structural, textural, optical, X-ray photoelectron, and Mössbauer characterization was combined with methylene blue removal experiments under adsorption, photocatalytic, Fenton-like, and photo-Fenton-like conditions. Both materials retained the MFI structure. UV–Vis analysis indicated a greater relative contribution of oligomeric FexOy species in Z0.4–Fe1.0. Mössbauer spectroscopy identified predominantly Fe3+ environments and revealed a magnetically ordered component in the high-iron material at 78 K. Despite an almost 28-fold difference in iron loading, both materials achieved nearly identical final methylene blue removal (~99%) under photo-Fenton-like conditions, yet this similar efficiency was reached through fundamentally different dominant pathways: predominantly adsorption for the microporous Z0–Fe0.1 (dark adsorption ~82%) and predominantly catalytic oxidation for the hierarchical Z0.4–Fe1.0 (dark adsorption only ~38%, rising to ~87% under dark Fenton-like conditions). These results indicate a shift in the balance between adsorption and H2O2-dependent removal accompanying changes in porosity and iron loading. The findings highlight the need to consider pore architecture, adsorption, and iron speciation jointly when interpreting the performance of Fe-containing zeolites for water treatment.

title: Modulation of low-molecular-weight cellulose self-assembly using a nonionic amphiphilic block copolymer
abstract: Abstract Artificial nanocelluloses constructed through the self-assembly of low-molecular-weight (LMW) cellulose have emerged as sustainable nanomaterials with tailorable nanomorphologies. Herein, we demonstrate the modulation of LMW cellulose self-assembly using Poloxamer 407 (P407), a poly(ethylene oxide)—poly(propylene oxide)—poly(ethylene oxide) triblock copolymer. LMW cellulose with average degrees of polymerization of approximately 7 and 10 formed nanosheets or nanoribbons in the presence of 15% and 20% (w/v) P407, while their dimensions and aggregation states varied markedly depending on the conditions. In particular, the former LMW cellulose formed nanosheets in intimate contact with one another with poorly defined boundaries at 15% (w/v) P407, while nanosheets with irregular, stepped edges were formed at 20% (w/v) P407. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry analyses suggested that P407 directly interacted with LMW cellulose and affected its self-assembly. These findings reveal that amphiphilic block copolymers can serve as effective modulators of LMW cellulose self-assembly and expand strategies for controlling the nanomorphologies of artificial nanocelluloses without chemical modification of cellulose molecules.
